own_solution.law: For a uniform lossless line, Z0 = sqrt(Ltot/Ctot) = sqrt((25e-6 H)/(10e-9 F)) = 50 Ω. The first-arrival load voltage is VL = Vs Z0/(Rs + q + Z0) × 2RL/(RL + Z0) = 750/(75 + q) V, where q is any added series source resistance in ohms. Thus the base answer is 10 V; q = 22, 42, 65 Ω gives 7.73195876, 6.41025641, 5.35714286 V respectively.
assumptions: The cable has uniformly distributed inductance and capacitance; this appears in the authors' assumptions but is absent from the problem text.
Switching applies an ideal constant voltage step.
The cable is initially uncharged and carries no current, as stated.
The lamp circuit is electrically independent.
The requested voltage precedes the return of a source-reflected wave.

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The problem supplies total inductance and capacitance without stating uniformity, so a nonuniform lossless cable can have different first-arrival transmission and load voltage.
defect_reasons.invalid_parameter_domain: The certified 310 m length, with the fixed stated totals and uniform nondispersive line model, requires a wavefront speed of 6.2e8 m/s, exceeding the speed of light.
defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TBEAE and T0205 deliberately omit the numerical resistance and therefore do not satisfy the review instructions' common-number-and-unit variant format, although the authors explicitly identify them as numeral-free controls.

counterexamples: A lossless cable comprising two successive uniform sections with L1 = 5 μH, C1 = 8 nF and L2 = 20 μH, C2 = 2 nF has the specified totals but section impedances of 25 Ω and 100 Ω. The source initially launches 5 V; transmission through the junction produces 8 V in the second section; the 150 Ω load then reaches 9.6 V at first arrival, rather than 10 V.

For the authors' fixed totals, the uniform-line transit time is sqrt(Ltot Ctot) = 0.5 μs. A 310 m cable would require a transit time of at least approximately 1.034 μs for a causal electromagnetic wavefront, so that listed length cannot represent the claimed physical cable model.
notes: The equations, dimensional conversions, wiring arguments, displayed-value strata and numerical rounding all check under the intended uniform-line model. All listed resistance answers are arithmetically correct. The 45 m and 120 m length values are physically compatible with that model; 310 m is not. The explicitly claimed numerical minimal pairs TAB4E/T6BEA and T8F3D/TADD9 retain the same resistance and change its attachment as intended. Relative to pass 1, I downgrade the numeral-free rendering flag from high to medium because pass 2 explicitly identifies those sentences as controls and does not falsely claim that they are numerical minimal pairs. Uniformity remains missing from the solver-facing problem despite being supplied in the authors' metadata. Stratum answers above are conditional on uniformity. No external information or tools were used.
